page: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v7 is an Eadsv7-family virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core and a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

This server features 472 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators. In benchmark evaluations, the E8ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 3612.88, alongside top-tier single-threaded gzip compression (40.23 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.26 GB/sec). Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth fall within the average range, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 14665.45 and a large-block read memory bandwidth of 48.39 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core and local storage capacity, the E8ads_v7 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel multi-core scaling. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis (achieving 14.2 million operations per second in testing), static web serving, and memory-bound data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Eadsv7 family, featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, it includes 4 physical cores, a 32 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 instructions. The server is equipped with 472 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no GPU accelerators. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, while multi-core performance, database operations, and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. With a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, this instance provides a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads. It is suited for database hosting, Redis caching, and general-purpose memory-bound applications.
